drivingQuestion: How does the mishna's sleep oath square with R' Yohanan?
outcomeNote: the contradiction of the previous unit is resolved by distinguishing cases

segments.en: The Gemara answers: «There,» Rabbi Yoḥanan is referring to a case «where he said» explicitly that he will not sleep for «three» days. «Here,» the mishna is referring to a case «where he did not say three» days, and his oath extends only for the amount of time it is possible not to sleep.

moves.summary: there he said three days, here he did not
moves.about: R' Yohanan speaks of one who said 'three days'; the mishna of one who did not

edges.cueHe: התם דאמר שלשה, הכא דלא אמר שלשה
edges.about: R' Yohanan speaks of one who said 'three days'; the mishna of one who did not

positions.claim: R' Yohanan's case specifies three days; the mishna's does not, and is limited to possible duration
